title: Quentin and the Salt
premise: In the salt-locked city of Greyharbor, magic is outlawed and old gods have gone silent, but beast-speaker Coral Voss has quietly kept his gift alive through five years of small charms and smaller lies. When prayers begin to be answered again, Coral discovers the court beneath the mountain has been hoarding stolen souls to fuel its claim on divinity — including the soul of his late sister, sold by a debt-broker years ago. Guided by a dying dragon's last fire and a salt-witch who remembers the gods' true names, Coral descends beneath the mountain, bargains with a corrupting court that offers him power in exchange for silence, and finally steals back his sister's soul at the cost of his own gift. In the end, the dragon-fire gutters out, the court's stolen divinity collapses, and Coral returns to Greyharbor mortal but unhidden — belonging, at last, to no one's law but his own.
about_author: Tamsin Nakamura is a former tide-pool surveyor who grew up between a fishing village and her grandmother's shrine room, where stories were currency more reliable than coin. She writes fantasy about quiet people keeping forbidden things alive.

chapters.title: The Year of Answered Prayers
chapters.summary: Coral Voss's POV. In outlawed Greyharbor, Coral sells charms by day and speaks to gulls by night, hiding his gift even from himself. When a drowned fisherman's widow reports her prayer was answered by something ancient, Coral realizes the silent gods are waking — and that his own small magics may have lit the fuse. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in longing, the terror of being seen.

chapters.title: What the Salt Remembers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with interludes from the salt-witch Maren. A dying dragon named Vess calls Coral by name, revealing that souls sold to the court beneath the mountain are powering its false divinity — including his sister Wren's. Maren teaches him the old names hidden in tide-salt, but warns that the court corrupts all who bargain. Emotional beat: grief transformed into purpose; memory as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Descending through Vess's guttering fire-light, Coral infiltrates the soul-vaults and confronts the Undercourt, which offers him his sister's freedom plus godhood if he betrays Maren and the waking gods. He witnesses what power has made of them: beautiful, hollow, starving. When he refuses, they seize Wren's soul-cage and hunt him through the dark. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive, then defiance at its loneliest.

chapters.title: The Last Fire
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, closing with Maren's. As Vess's flame dies, Coral breaks the vault using the true names in the salt, freeing every stolen soul — Wren's among them — though the effort burns out his gift forever. The Undercourt's divinity collapses inward; the mountain exhales. Coral surfaces into grey dawn, ordinary at last, and the city's people gather around him not as a criminal but as one of their own. Emotional beat: costly victory, and belonging earned rather than hidden.
